---
title: "Mensis Mirabilis"
date: 2026-09-01
categories: [Non-technical]
toc: false   # no section headings in this post, so no "On this page" box
---

It seems as if we are on the eve of the singularity and something deep about the
world would need to break for us to not have superhuman intelligence within the
next five years. This blog is my way of trying to organise my thoughts and
contribute to the discourse at this moment in history. I plan to focus on the
shape of AI research and development, the diffusion of AI through society and
the economy, safety and control of frontier AI systems and how AI changes what
it means to be human.

I’m not entirely sure what to think about most of the questions I will address
and I make no claim that these opinions are final. Intellectual inquiry is not
merely some sequence of Bayesian updates. It is extremely difficult to even
specify our hypothesis space, figure out whether we are asking the right
questions or know what an answer is. Trying to do so will require me to take
ideas seriously, sometimes too seriously, and lead me to positions I do not
hold.

It’s a shame to have a post that introduces a blog without a single idea. So,
here is one. Throughout history, brilliant minds have been unusually productive
over short time spans. Isaac Newton developed calculus, optics and gravitation
over the course of eighteen months. Einstein explained special relativity,
Brownian motion and the photoelectric effect over four. Historians call this an
*annus mirabilis* or miracle year. Engineers from Anthropic claim that Mythos
Preview led to a
[4x uplift](https://www.anthropic.com/institute/recursive-self-improvement)
in their work. That means today, a miracle month — a *mensis mirabilis* — is now
possible.[^1]

[^1]: Of course, the *mensis mirabilis* will primarily occur for fields where
    models are already good (such as AI development and code generation). It
    doesn’t seem so far-fetched that (say) a blog writer could have a *mensis
    mirabilis* or something similar to that.
